errorCodes.meaning: No such transport is configured on this agent.
The caller is not a super-admin.

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.
Ext.title: Ext

ServiceKind.description: Which transport a task is acting on. This is the discriminator: it selects which member of `config` is meaningful, and a payload naming one kind with another's config is malformed rather than merely ignored.
ServiceKind.title: ServiceKind

ServiceMutationResult.description: The outcome of a change to an advertised service. Every member describes the **log entry the change produced**, because that is what the change actually is: the agent's DID document is the record, and a consumer that treats the response as a mere acknowledgement will miss that a redeploy may be required.

drainEndsAt.description: Present when the change scheduled a DIDComm drain. Its absence means no drain was scheduled, NOT that a drain finished instantly: a consumer reporting 'done' on an absent value would be right, and one reporting it on a present value would be wrong.

drainingMediator.description: The mediator being drained, when `drainEndsAt` is present.

effectiveAt.description: RFC 3339 instant the change took effect — the same instant stamped on the new log entry.

logEntryVersionId.description: Version id of the new did:webvh log entry this change wrote. Joins the change to the document's history.

serverless.description: True when the agent's DID is self-hosted. **The change is persisted locally but NOT published**: the operator must fetch the updated `did.jsonl` and redeploy before any verifier sees it. A consumer that ignores this reports success for a change no one else can observe yet.

vtaDid.description: The agent's own DID — subject of the log entry this change wrote. Carried so a caller can follow up without a second round trip.

schema.description: Request payload for vta/services/disable. Stops advertising a transport and republishes the log. For `didcomm` this schedules a drain rather than cutting delivery immediately — see `drainEndsAt` in the result.

drainTtlSeconds.description: `didcomm` only: how long the unadvertised mediator keeps accepting delivery. Absent takes the agent's default. **0 means immediate teardown, and is only honoured when the request did not arrive through the mediator being torn down** — over a DIDComm-carried request the agent enforces a floor (1 hour), because cutting the mediator mid-request would discard the reply to the very task asking for it. A caller cannot rely on 0 being obeyed; read `drainEndsAt` in the result to learn what actually happened.

schema.title: VTA Services — Disable — payload
